the cited behaviour is re-read against the code at implementation time: pipeline.py:593-600 and resolve_mode carrying no margin. If either has moved, the citation is corrected before the fix is written rather than after

this is the only finding from the 2026-09-20 pass that bears on the product's single invariant -- no spoken command acts in strict mode -- so it is not an ergonomics issue and does not belong in a frame about operator convenience

the fix touches the mode-resolution path only. If a change here would alter which utterances are LABELLED commands, it is out of this frame and the golden set must be re-run -- this frame moves the boundary, never the labelling

a decision whose utterance BEGAN inside a strict window is judged by the window in force when speech STARTED, not when the decision completed; the joiner already tracks speech_started to speech_stopped, so the timestamp needed is in hand

speech_started is actually available on the utterance the pipeline receives. If the joiner drops it, threading it through is part of this work and not a separate frame -- and if it is unavailable for a reconnect-orphaned utterance, that utterance takes the stricter of the two modes
fail toward the stricter column, consistent with the clock-trust rule: where the two boundaries disagree, the strict reading wins

fail-toward-strict is implemented as the explicit rule, not as an accident of ordering: a test asserts that an utterance spanning a boundary in EITHER direction is judged strict, so a later refactor cannot silently reverse it

the household speaking Hebrew in the room during the minutes around a window boundary -- candle lighting and tzeit -- who do not know a boundary is near and are not adjusting their speech for it. Secondarily whoever audits the core invariant, for whom this frame is the record that the boundary was examined rather than assumed.
the boundary tests name real clock instants for the configured location rather than synthetic offsets, so a zmanim change is visible as a test failure instead of passing against an arbitrary number

a command's verdict is fixed by the mode in force when its speech STARTED, so the refusal a strict window promises holds for every utterance the window contained, regardless of when the decision completed. Where the start-time mode and the decision-time mode disagree, the strict reading wins. No clock margin, sleep or grace period is introduced -- the timestamp comes from the joiner's speech_started, which already exists.
no sleep, margin or grace period is introduced -- the fix is a different TIMESTAMP, not a delay; a margin would trade one silent boundary error for another

a test that pins the clock across tzeit and asserts a command whose speech began inside the window is REFUSED while the same command begun two seconds after the window is ACTED on -- the pair, not either alone, because passing only the first is satisfiable by always refusing. Plus the mirror pair at the window-OPEN boundary, which must keep failing safe as it does today.
both halves of each pair are asserted in the same test, so a future change cannot delete the acts-case and leave a refuses-case that passes vacuously

4 of 4 boundary cases pass, and 0 of the golden set's strict-mode hard false positives appear -- the release-blocking number stays 0 across all 295 rows after the change, because moving the boundary must not move the labelling.
the golden set is actually re-run against the real model, not assumed unaffected -- 'the change is only about timing' is precisely the kind of reasoning the 2026-09-20 pass found wrong four times

risks.text: this is the only plan in the set that edits the gate path itself. A mistake here fails SILENTLY -- a command that acts on Shabbat looks exactly like a hint that acted -- so the usual signal that something is wrong does not exist. The mitigation is that t3's four cases run before t4 and the whole thing merges as one small diff touching no labelling code.

the 295-row bound is evidence about typed and synthesised input only -- the golden set has NEVER been run against this room's acoustics (frame park v5). A pass here therefore re-establishes the existing bound after the change; it does not establish that the bound holds in this room, and the report must not be read as if it did.
the four-case boundary test is the natural place to later add the acoustic entrance once v5's golden-set run against this room happens -- the instants and the fixtures will already exist.

the 15s strict_mode_delay is untouched here. It does not help at this boundary because the mode has already flipped by the time the delay runs, and whether 15s satisfies the deliberate-delay premise at all is parked in the frame (v2) and in docs/halacha-open-questions.md.

t4 is an assignment an agent has every reason to dislike, and that is itself a risk to the measurement rather than a matter of morale: 295 rows against a live model, minutes of waiting, no code written, no visible progress, and the one instruction that matters says do not reason your way out of running it. The cheapest way to 'finish' t4 is to conclude that a timing change cannot affect labelling and report green -- which is exactly the proxy-for-property failure that occurred four times on 2026-09-20. Tracked here so the assignment is honest about what it asks: the disincentive is structural, it points at under-running rather than at refusal, and the countermeasure is that t4's acceptance criteria demand the report name the stack it ran against, which a skipped run cannot produce.

the fan-out is degenerate for this plan: waves are 1-1-1-1, so the workforce leg buys no parallelism and costs four sequential worktree create/merge/remove cycles. It is run for the isolation and the TDD gate at each step, not for speed, and a later plan in this set (hearing-correctness) is where the parallel form actually pays. Recorded so the choice is visible rather than looking like an unexamined default.

BLOCKING, and it is not caused by this plan: the golden set run on UNMODIFIED code (pre-t1, commit c2efa53, prompt p2, senses = nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4, gateway 0.81.0) reports hard_false_positives(text/strict) = 14 of 230 hard rows, plus wrong_actions = 11. The release-blocking threshold is 0 and CLAUDE.md says a HARD failure blocks a release and must not be tuned. So t4's acceptance criterion 'hard_false_positives_strict is 0' CANNOT be met by finishing this plan -- the number is already 14 before the boundary fix exists. Two of the failures are unambiguous strict-mode invariant breaks on request-shaped wishes: k-c45_06 'halevai shemishehu yadlik et hamazgan' (I wish someone would turn on the AC) and k-c45_08 (I would be glad if the AC were on), both act_strict=false, both ACTED. Six are fragments that must not act and did, four are mixed command+hint rows with intent=none that must not act in EITHER mode and did. The agent is deployed live with --apply on this box.

t3's test pins the joiner's wall clock by assigning the private pipeline.joiner._wall_clock, because Pipeline exposes joiner_clock (the monotonic receive clock) but no seam for the joiner's wall_clock. It works and the test asserts last_utterance_start.wall_time to prove the pinned instant is the one the joiner handed downstream, but a private-attribute assignment in a test is a missing public seam: a joiner_wall_clock parameter on Pipeline would be the honest fix. Recorded rather than silently accepted, and deliberately not done here because 'prefer a test to a product change' applied.

t3 found a real hole in its own acceptance criterion 3 and closed it: using the REAL zmanim computation alone would let a zmanim change move both edges of the window together and the test would still pass, because the test derives its instants from the same computation it is checking. That is a proxy standing in for the property -- the exact defect this frame exists around. The fix was to anchor both edges against the independent published Hebcal vectors in tests/fixtures/zmanim_sun_vectors.json within the repo's 2-minute tolerance. The anchors are part of how criterion 3 is met, not decoration; removing them silently weakens the test to tautology.
